title: Bohemian Rhapsody
tagline: Four lads, one farmhouse, a lot of cheese on toast.
about: A young baggage handler from Feltham joins a London band and becomes one of the great showmen in rock history.
cue: Serve the rarebit when the band hole up at the farmhouse studio in Wales to make the new album.
faces: LONDON. TWENTY MINUTES ON STAGE, THE WHOLE WORLD WATCHING.
SERVED IN THE GRANDSTAND WITH FULL HONOURS.
Toasted sourdough under a grilled sauce of sharp cheddar, mustard, milk and egg yolk.
Parsi fried chicken marinated in ginger, garlic, chilli and spice, crumbed in semolina and egg.
Parsi family lamb dhansak with brown rice
Lamb simmered in a spiced dal of lentils, pumpkin.
Fish in banana leaf with green coconut chutney.
Parsi wedding custard of reduced milk, condensed milk, eggs, cardamom and nutmeg.
Cold lager topped half and half with lemonade, with a lemon wedge, in a chilled pint glass
Pimm's cup with cucumber and mint
A toast to Mary, just next door.
Piano's set and the meters are taped down. Feed the crew before the gates open, nobody gets a sandwich once the band's on.
On the big screen tonight: Loading suitcases at Heathrow. The coffee machine Roger nearly throws.

    StartersRockfield farm Welsh rarebitToasted sourdough under a grilled sauce of sharp cheddar, mustard, milk and egg yolk, with cayenne and spring onionHow to make it30g butter2 tbsp plain flour150ml milk250g sharp cheddar, grated2 tsp English mustard1 egg yolk1 pinch of cayenne pepper1/2 tsp ground black pepper8 thick slices of sourdough2 spring onions, slicedMelt the butter, stir in the flour for a minute, then whisk in the milk until thick.Off the heat stir in the cheddar, mustard, egg yolk, cayenne and pepper.Toast the sourdough on one side under the grill, turn and spread thickly with the cheese mixture.Grill until bubbling and blistered, scatter with spring onion and serve hot.Bulsara kitchen chicken farchaParsi fried chicken marinated in ginger, garlic, chilli and spice, crumbed in semolina and egg, with lemon and mango chutneyHow to make it1kg chicken drumettes and wings2 tbsp ginger garlic paste1 lemon, half juiced, half in wedges2 tsp ground cumin1 tsp ground turmeric2 tsp chilli powder1 tsp garam masala1 tsp salt60g fine semolina60g dried breadcrumbs3 eggs, beaten500ml vegetable oil, for frying120g mango chutneyMix the ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, cumin, turmeric, chilli powder, garam masala and salt and rub into the chicken.Cover and marinate in the fridge.Roll each piece in the semolina and breadcrumbs, dip in the beaten eggs and roll again.Shallow-fry in 2cm of oil at 170°C in batches, turning, until deep golden and cooked through. Drain on paper towel.Serve hot with lemon wedges and the chutney.MainsParsi family lamb dhansak with brown riceLamb simmered in a spiced dal of lentils, pumpkin, eggplant and tamarind, with caramelised onion brown rice and kachumberHow to make it1kg lamb shoulder, diced1 cup toor dal, rinsed1/2 cup red lentils, rinsed300g butternut pumpkin, peeled and diced1 small eggplant, diced2 tomatoes, chopped2 brown onions, 1 chopped, 1 thinly sliced for the rice2 tbsp ginger garlic paste2 green chillies, slit2 tbsp dhansak masala or garam masala1 tsp ground turmeric1 tsp ground cumin1 tbsp tamarind paste1 tbsp brown sugar1 bunch coriander, chopped4 tbsp ghee2 cups basmati rice, rinsed1 tbsp sugar, for the brown rice1 cinnamon stick2 tsp salt1 red onion, finely chopped1 Lebanese cucumber, diced1 tomato, diced, for the kachumber1 lime, juicedBrown the lamb in 2 tbsp of the ghee in batches and lift out.Fry the chopped onion until golden, add the ginger garlic paste, chillies, masala and cumin and cook 2 minutes.Return the lamb with the toor dal, red lentils, pumpkin, eggplant, tomatoes, turmeric and 1.5 litres water. Cover and simmer until the lamb is soft.Lift out the lamb, blend the dal roughly, return the lamb with the tamarind, brown sugar and half the salt and simmer 10 minutes.For the rice, fry the sliced onion in the rest of the ghee until deep brown, add the sugar and let it caramelise, then add the cinnamon, rice, the rest of the salt and 3 cups water. Cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, then rest 5.Toss the red onion, cucumber and tomato with the lime juice and a pinch of salt for the kachumber.Scatter the dhansak with coriander and serve with the brown rice and the kachumber.Jer Bulsara's patra ni machhiFish in banana leaf with green coconut chutney, from his mother's tableHow to make it4 firm white fish fillets, about 150g each60g desiccated coconut1 bunch coriander1 small bunch mint2 green chillies3 garlic cloves1 tsp ground cumin1 tsp sugar2 limes4 pieces of banana leaf or baking paperSoak the coconut in 3 tbsp hot water for 5 minutes, then blend with the herbs, chillies, garlic, cumin, sugar, juice of a lime and salt to a thick paste.Soften the banana leaf over a flame or in hot water.Coat each fillet thickly in chutney and wrap in a piece of leaf, tied with string.Steam over simmering water until the fish flakes.Serve in the leaf with lime wedges to open at the table.SweetsLagan nu custardParsi wedding custard of reduced milk, condensed milk, eggs, cardamom and nutmeg, baked golden under flaked almondsHow to make it1 L full cream milk395g tin condensed milk4 eggs1/2 tsp ground cardamom1 whole nutmeg, for grating1 tsp vanilla extract10g butter, for the dish40g flaked almondsSimmer the milk in a wide pan, stirring often, until reduced by about a third.Stir in the condensed milk and cool a little.Heat the oven to 160°C and butter a 20cm baking dish. Whisk in the eggs, cardamom, a grating of nutmeg and vanilla, then strain into the dish.Scatter with the almonds and bake in a water bath until just set and golden on top.Cool a little before serving, or chill.DrinksWembley summer shandyCold lager topped half and half with lemonade, with a lemon wedge, in a chilled pint glassHow to make it4 x 375ml bottles of lager1.5 L cold lemonade1 lemon, in wedgesChill the lager, lemonade and glasses well.Half fill each glass with lager, tilting the glass.Top with lemonade and drop in a lemon wedge.Pimm's cup with cucumber and mintA toast to Mary, just next door.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
